title: Cryptool vs Allocations
content_html:
Cryptool vs Allocations
=======================

If you need institutional-grade cap table management, fund accounting, and compliance for a regulated fund, Allocations is the better choice. If you require a non-custodial, crypto-focused system that handles portfolio tracking, capital raising, syndicate management, and OTC trading across multiple blockchains, Cryptool.io is the better fit.

What Allocations is good at

Allocations focuses on the back office of fund management. Its core strength is cap table management: issuing and tracking equity, tokens, and hybrid securities across multiple share classes with waterfall calculations, pro-rata rights, and transfer restrictions. The platform handles investor onboarding with identity verification, accredited investor checks, and subscription document management. Fund accounting features include NAV calculation, performance reporting, and audit-ready financials. Allocations also provides an investor portal where LPs can view holdings, download K-1s, and sign documents. For managers running regulated funds across traditional and crypto assets, Allocations delivers the compliance and accounting infrastructure that auditors and administrators expect.

What Cryptool does differently

Cryptool.io starts from the investment side and extends into fund operations. Portfolio tracking covers every wallet and chain non-custodially: connect MetaMask, Ledger, Trust Wallet, or any other provider once and see balances, unrealised P/L, staking positions, and vesting schedules in one dashboard. Capital raising runs end to end: create a pool, set caps and vesting schedules, collect commitments with identity verification, and distribute tokens automatically when unlocks occur. Syndicate management lets you create investment groups with tiered allocations, track per-member positions, and run distributions without moving funds through Cryptool. The OTC marketplace matches buyers and sellers for locked allocations, SAFTs, and other private assets with indicative quotes and best-efforts settlement. Investor reporting generates LP updates tied to live portfolio data. Calendar tracks vesting events, raise milestones, and portfolio dates with notifications. White-label deployment lets you run the platform under your own brand. All of this sits on a non-custodial foundation: Cryptool never holds keys, funds, or signing authority.

Which one should you pick

Pick Allocations if you run a regulated fund that needs institutional-grade cap table management, fund accounting, NAV calculations, and audit-ready financials across traditional and digital assets. Its investor onboarding, compliance workflows, and LP portal are built for the back-office requirements that administrators and auditors expect.

Pick Cryptool.io if you manage crypto-native investments and need the full lifecycle in one place: tracking wallets across every chain, running raises with vesting, managing syndicates with per-member allocations, trading locked positions OTC, and sending investor reports tied to live data. All without giving up custody.

Use both if your fund requires Allocations for cap table and accounting infrastructure while the investment team uses Cryptool for deal flow, portfolio visibility, raise execution, and distribution operations. The two platforms solve adjacent problems and can complement each other in a hybrid fund stack.

FAQ

What is the main difference between Cryptool and Allocations?

Allocations is a fund administration platform focused on cap tables, fund accounting, and investor compliance. Cryptool.io is a crypto investment operating system that combines portfolio tracking, fundraising, syndicate management, OTC trading, vesting, and investor reporting in one non-custodial workspace.

Does Allocations support multi-chain portfolio tracking?

Not a focus. Allocations is built for fund administration and cap table management rather than live wallet aggregation across chains.

Can Cryptool replace a fund administrator?

Cryptool provides investor reporting, allocation tracking, and distribution automation, but it does not perform fund accounting, NAV calculation, or audit-ready financials. Most institutional funds use a dedicated administrator alongside Cryptool.

Does Allocations have an OTC marketplace for locked allocations?

Not a focus. Allocations does not offer a secondary trading venue for unvested or locked positions.

Is Cryptool non-custodial?

Yes. Cryptool never holds private keys, funds, or signing authority. Wallet connections are read-only. Every transaction is signed by the user's own wallet.

Which platform is better for running a crypto syndicate?

Cryptool.io includes syndicate management with tiered member allocations, pool creation, automated distributions, and an investor portal. Allocations does not focus on syndicate operations.

Can I use Cryptool for investor onboarding and identity verification?

Yes. Cryptool includes identity verification for participants during a raise, along with commitment tracking and investor communications through its CRM features.

Does Allocations offer white-label deployment?

Not a focus. Allocations is typically deployed as a branded fund administration platform rather than a white-labelled product for managers to rebrand.
